alt: Two magnets attract with unlike poles and repel with like poles; a magnet attracts unmagnetised iron at either pole and never repels it, so only repulsion proves both are magnets. Touching the end of bar X to the middle of bar Y: strong attraction means X is the magnet; little or none means Y is the magnet, because a magnet's middle has almost no magnetic effect.
caption: Only repulsion proves both are magnets; the end-to-middle test separates magnet from iron.

alt: Left: a chain of soft-iron nails hangs from a magnet and falls apart as soon as the magnet is removed, because soft iron is a temporary magnet. Right: a chain of steel pins stays partly stuck together after the magnet is removed, because steel keeps its magnetism.
caption: Soft iron when the magnetism must switch off; steel when it must stay.

alt: Left: small plotting compasses around a bar magnet point along the field, their N ends showing its direction from the N pole round to the S pole; marking and joining the positions draws a field line. Right: iron filings show the whole pattern at once but give no direction.
caption: Compasses show direction; filings show only the shape of the pattern.
